cohort: The study included women who experienced sterilization failure and sought care at a Government Medical College and Hospital over a ten-year period.
finding: The study found that tuboperitoneal fistula was the leading cause of sterilization failure (45.6%), with failures most common in the 25-29 age group and frequently originating from Primary Health Centers.
mod_finding: LSCS-based sterilizations were a common type of procedure contributing to failure, and ectopic pregnancies were significantly more prevalent following minilap procedures (79%) compared to laparoscopic methods (14%).
